text.text:
If The Cheesecake Factory has no fans then I’m probably gone. With that being said I truly love it here. The food quality is so good and it never misses. The decor is nice but it does tend to get quite loud in the afternoon/ evening, I haven’t checked them out during their brunch hours. Service can sometimes be slow bc everyone is SO busy but it’s definitely worth paying a visit!! I love you Cheesecake Factory

My top dishes
buffalo chicken blasts: very sizable and big portion with a crisp exterior with a very decent amount of filling (not too salty and def ask for extra blue cheese in the side)

avocado egg rolls: no notes. Fantastic. The avocado is perfectly ripe and ugh so GOOD, you just need to try it.

Mac and cheese balls: Coming from a lactose intolerant person these are definitely worth getting, I thought they were overrated until I tried them and my lord these were SO good. I think the vodka sauce instead of marinara gives it a ✨je ne sais quoi✨ (but it’s kind of heavy so def share)

Louisiana chicken pasta: MY FAVORITE!!!! spicy and saucy with crisp Parmesan breaded chicken and mushrooms omg this is hands down amazing.

chicken picatta with angel hair pasta and EXTRA sauce on the side: I love me a picatta and this did not disappoint but I wonder how it would’ve tasted if I had crispy chicken. Still delicious though, perfect amount of lemon and capers

Top cheesecakes: Vanilla bean, dulce de leche, and the original. Honorable mention: Linda’s fudge cake!

⭐ Disappointing First Impression – Terraza 7
I purchased a ticket in advance to visit Terraza 7, and unfortunately, my experience ended before I even entered the restaurant.
When we arrived, the area and the exterior of the place were very different from what I expected based on the photos I had seen online. I felt uncomfortable and unsafe enough that I decided not to get out of my car. We ended up leaving and going somewhere else.
What made it more disappointing was that I had already paid for the ticket. I understand that online photos can present a place differently, but the difference between what I expected and what I encountered upon arrival was significant.
I can’t comment on the food, music, or service because we chose not to enter. I’m simply sharing my experience as a paying customer who arrived but did not feel comfortable enough to go inside.
Unfortunately, I felt that the money I spent on the ticket was wasted. I hope Terraza 7 can provide potential customers with a clearer and more realistic impression of the location and entrance so people know what to expect before purchasing tickets.

text.text: Enjoyed a really spectacular dinner at il Gigante earlier this week. I’d walked past a few times and had been curious to find a solid Italian spot near me in Bushwick, and boy did they deliver. The interior of the restaurant is very cozy and chic, great vibes for a date night. We had the tricolore salad to start, which was delicious and enough for 3 people, along with an embarrassing amount of their house focaccia which is superb. For mains, I ordered the pappardelle with wild boar ragu (seriously good), and my friends had the cacio e pepe (tasty, albeit a small-ish portion) and the seafood spaghetti (my favorite bite of the night—exceptionally toothsome and rich). We also split the brussel sprouts and fingerling potatoes, both good but I’d stick to ordering another app or pasta next time. We were unfortunately too full for dessert, but we were treated to an excellent limoncello digestif which hit the spot. Service was on point all around, and at half (less?) the price I’d pay for a comparable meal in Manhattan it’s a superb value. Will be back again and again!

Barriles is a wonderful place to eat, drink and hang out with friends or family.

A couple of us stopped by to watch some games here (they have a ton of TVs) and were taken care of by Paola and the manager Jenny. They were amazing and attentive, we loved the people here. The menu is very large and offers a bit of everything for everyone. The salmon, steak and burger we ordered were all great, and the apps were amazing.

We didn’t drink on this occasion but they literally have bars on each side and a large selection of drinks.

It’s a sports bar, so expect the whole shabang of drinks, TVs and crowd, especially during futbol or basketball. Price wise I would say it’s a premium but you do pay for quality and a better ambiance, which is fair.

Parking is street and relatively easy to find, didn’t take us long during dinner time.

Definitely going to be coming here during the World Cup. Crowd and food were great and recommend to those looking for authentic Colombian food and drinks.

I used to come here often with my dad when I was young &very ill. I happened to be in the area and popped in to remember the good times and taste the food which I remember being really good and I remember was one of the only places that didn’t make me sick. For starters there is no visible menu displayed, only paper menus so I didn’t know how to order since my dad used to order for me when I was a child. The establishment was nearly empty and there was one person behind me, also waiting to be served right after me. The young man at the register was very pleasant and presented me with the paper menu when he noticed I was confused. I had questions but he ultimately kept insisting I should ask the person on the line putting the food together. When I handed my receipt I expressed to him I hadn’t been there in a long time, so I wasn’t clear in how to order. The man seemed instantly irritated by my question. I asked him what were the options to add into my pita and he made a motion to the toppings on the buffet counter. When I politely asked him what it was he was reluctant to tell me the names and only told me what the items were that I pointed at. The pita comes with a salad, which were pre-packed and not marked. He asked me which salad did I want and I told him I didn’t know since I didn’t know what they were. When I said that, he quickly moved on to preparing the food for the lady standing behind me on line. As I looked at the salad options I noticed most of the salad options seemed to have a small greenish yellow jalapeño in them, but I had never seen them so small and that color before, so I didn’t want to assume since I’ve never seen or tried that kind of food other than when I was younger and my dad would order for me. So I asked if that was a jalapeño and he responded “what does it look like?” With an attitude. So I told him “well you haven’t told me what these are and I can’t eat food that’s too spicy” to which he responded “well they’re jalapeños so of course it’ll be spicy.” So I asked what wasn’t spicy, to which he pointed a the only option. I told him I’ll take that. He quickly tossed the pre-packed red cabbage salad and packed my food in a bag for me to take it and left it on the counter. He quickly proceeded to continue his conversation with the lady behind me who had already fished her order and packed her food. I noticed the distinct demeanor and I told him “I haven’t been here in 10 years. It would be nice if you could be nicer and patient and explain what I’m ordering..” and he walked away towards the register while I was mid sentence. I was very disappointed to see that a fellow Latino would be so impolite. So I spoke to him in Spanish and said “you’re nice to the white lady next to me but you treat me differently and that’s not right” to which he again walked away and left me talking mid sentence. I then quickly grabbed some napkins and left the store. As soon as I walked out of the store he conveniently went back to his post.
All in all, I will most definitely not be returning. It was disappointing and disheartening to see how uncomfortable I was made to feel. No good food is worth being made to feel small.

Pros: Delicious food and drinks. Enormous portions. Each dish can feed at least 2 people.  Greetings from the executive chef and decent service overall.

Cons: Prices are slightly higher than they should be. Paying close to 40 dollars for pasta (handmade, and a show) still seems steep.
As mentioned above the service was decent. Could be warmer with letting the diners eat without having to constantly ask to remove “possible empty plates” where they have food on them.

Lastly, almost none of the servers were wearing masks and that creates too much room for error. For that reason, I’m out.

-Suggestion would be to give a heads up (about the masks) for those making reservations in advance. (Even if there’s no mandate)

Overall, I would recommend this for those able to splurge a bit on a definitely unique experience.

Side note: noticed a slight price increase already from what the menu says online. For a restaurant that just opened.

-Suggestion would be to give the community time to acclimate and build up a reputation before making that leap.

Good luck to pier26! Hope you succeed the best that you can.

This up and coming place is worth a visit. The chef is an artist and the restaurant is his gallery. If your a seafood lover, you can’t go wrong with any of the entrees here. If you’re not that into seafood, try the fresh Alfredo spaghetti with table side cheese block service. You have to see it to understand, and then you get to taste it, and it’s truly wonderful. From the amount of times we saw the pasta / cheese cart exit the kitchen for the tableside performance, it must be a popular choice.

Move over chicken and waffles, there’s a seafood version here that’s a work of art and delicious.

Leave room for dessert. There are many interesting and unique choices like midnight munchies, strawberry cheesecake, and a chocolate mousse ball thingy. Lots of free on street parking in the area.

Family friendly and also good for couples. You might need a reservation as this place grows in popularity.

text.text:
This kosher (under supervision of VHQ) restaurant is a  high end , white table cloth dairy restaurant specializing  in fish and pasta. The menu is very "foodie" oriented, with many unusual items . Some of them work very well, others not so much. I was very glad to see this type of restaurant opened on Main Street, as there was no high end place to take a client or for family events.

The decor is beautiful , as you can see from the pictures. It's not too loud- the restaurant was about half full when I was there and you could have a conversation without screaming. The background music was a little loud for my taste, but it wasn't too annoying.

Service was very good- the waitress clearly knew the menu and was able to answer our questions. Their is an extensive wine and spirit list, but surprisingly , no beer availability. I have been to several kosher restaurants with several types of craft beer : perhaps they haven't gotten around to it yet.

I had the Branzino, with corn chowder. The  fish was too heavily fried. The frying seems to cover the flavor- essentially it was like a very expensive ($44) fried fish sandwich. However, the corn chowder was great-very complex, with lots of different flavors that worked together very well.

My wife had as an appetizer the Ninja Star appetizer, which was also overly fried. Other people who have eaten at the restaurant have said their entree was fried and greasy. I didn't find my meal too greasy but it was definitely heavily fried.

I love that a restaurant comes in and tries all kinds of interesting, unusual dishes- it's not surprising not all of them work.  I hope the restaurant is successful.  I plan to come again soon.
